commands.name: start
commands.description: Onboard a host end-to-end (SSH first-touch → bootstrap → verify online). Never prompts: supply the SSH password via --password-stdin, --prompt-password (explicit opt-in), or $BRIDGE_SSH_PASSWORD; with none of these the host is assumed to already trust the bridge key. The password is sent once in the request body, never on argv. The UI onboard form is the equivalent browser path.

flags.description: SSH host to onboard (hostname or IP)

flags.description: Existing durable Machine identity to reconnect or retry. When omitted, a new Machine is created for first-time onboarding; Bridge never infers historic identity from a hostname.

flags.name: provision-sudo
flags.description: Install a scoped passwordless-sudo drop-in for the SSH user at first touch so later privileged steps work over non-interactive SSH (default: on)

flags.name: no-provision-sudo
flags.description: Do not install the passwordless-sudo drop-in (opt out of the default-on behaviour)

flags.name: source
flags.description: Source mode: pinned (default; node clones the pushed revision) or working-tree (ship the control plane's local tree over SSH so uncommitted work onboards without a commit or push). working-tree is the owner development/validation mode; its nodes record dirty provenance and are excluded from fleet rolls

flags.name: password-stdin
flags.description: Read the SSH password from stdin (pipe it from a secret manager or `read -s`); one trailing newline is stripped. Mutually exclusive with --prompt-password. The password is sent once in the request body — never on argv, never stored

flags.name: setup-passphrase-stdin
flags.description: Read one credential-store passphrase as the second stdin line after the SSH password; it is sent only through the bootstrap stdin channel and never stored

flags.name: prompt-password
flags.description: Ask for the SSH password with a masked interactive prompt (requires a TTY). Without this flag `start` never prompts. Mutually exclusive with --password-stdin

omitted.reason: Internal typed preparation used by onboarding protection and cleanup provisioning to resolve the target and publish its sealing key; operators invoke the resulting protected workflow rather than a standalone preparation command.
Node-facing authenticated event ingestion called by the node-agent while reporting cleanup progress; it is not an operator command.
Browser-facing enrollment RPC used to exchange a local public key for an enrollment record; it is an authenticated UI flow, not an operator CLI command.
Node-facing authenticated session output/close report called by the node-agent, not an operator. The agent reports interactive session frames on the channel.
Node-facing dial-out RPC called by the node-agent, not an operator. There is no `nodes heartbeat` command; the agent reports liveness/health on the channel.
Node-facing dial-out RPC called by the node-agent after receiving a signed server frame, not an operator. There is no operator delivery-ack command; the agent reports receipt on the channel.
Node-facing authenticated relay response called by the node-agent after executing a signed relay frame, not an operator. The owner-facing relay call is RelayService/Call.
Node-facing authenticated credential delivery receipt called by the node-agent; operators inspect the generation and ack metadata through grant inventory.
Node-facing dial-out RPC: the node-agent streams run events back here signed with its per-node credential. There is no operator `runs report` command; the agent reports run progress on the channel.

Node-facing dial-out RPC: the node-agent's privileged helper streams provision events back here signed with its per-node credential. There is no operator `provision report` command; the agent reports provisioning progress on the channel.
Browser-facing owner account-creation facade. The CLI supports sign-in for an existing owner but deliberately does not create accounts; registration remains the UI's guided first-run flow.
Node-facing authenticated upload called by the bridge agent after a typed job produces bounded evidence; there is no operator upload command.
Node-facing authenticated key-add exchange called by an already-paired agent at startup; it is not an operator command.
Node-facing polling RPC used by the bootstrap agent after RequestPairing; operators review the same request through the owner-facing pair list command.
Node-facing authenticated grant reconciliation called by the node-agent after channel connection; operators use the owner-facing grant commands.
Owner-facing grant authoring is exposed by the secrets-manager grants CLI and Trust console, not the bridge fleet transport CLI.
Owner-facing grant inventory is exposed by the secrets-manager grants CLI and Trust console, not the bridge fleet transport CLI.
Owner-facing grant revocation is exposed by the secrets-manager grants CLI and Trust console, not the bridge fleet transport CLI.
Owner-facing address rotation is exposed by the secrets-manager grants CLI and root credential provisioning fanout, not the bridge fleet transport CLI.
